summary: Port reproduces the Progress-flag chevron structure exactly (same 11 mirrored bands, same colour order, same mirror axis, resolution- and fps-independent) but runs the animation BACKWARDS — bands converge edge-to-centre instead of expanding centre-to-edge — is ~18% slower per cycle, and is ~5x too bright overall.
observations: Rig: strip, 60 px, no controls on either side (meta.json sides.orig.controls = [] and sides.port.controls = []; --probe-controls reported 'no settable controls' for both). Control surfaces match.

Both sides render cleanly: no compileError/runtimeError on any run, wantsSensors false on both, brightnessTrend 'steady' on both at 6 s, 60 s, 240 s and in a --skip 60 late window. Neither side dies, freezes or saturates.

STRUCTURE MATCHES. Both draw a strip mirror-symmetric about the pivot between px 29/30 (i <-> 60-i on both sides, verified from --dump t=0: orig[1]==orig[59], orig[3]==orig[57]; port[1]==port[59], port[3]==port[57]).

Both lay out exactly 11 colour bands per half-strip (~2.7 px each on 60 px), in the same cyclic order: purple, blue, green, yellow, orange, red, white, pink, light-blue, brown, black — i.e. the six rainbow stripes plus the five Progress chevron stripes.

Both are RESOLUTION-INDEPENDENT: at --pixels 120 both still show 11 bands per half at ~5.5 px each (orig run-lengths 6,5,5,6,5,6,5,6,5,6,5; port 5,6,5,6,5,6,5,6,5,5). No feature-count change with rig size on either side.
Both are SEED-INDEPENDENT and deterministic: t=0 frames at --seed 1234 are byte-identical to --seed 1 on both sides. No stochastic component to judge.

Both are FPS-INVARIANT (time-based, not frame-stepped). Tracking the orange band on the left half from t=0: orig 11 -> 0 px over 2.5 s at 10, 20 and 40 fps alike; port 17 -> 26/27 px over 2.5 s at all three rates. No frame-rate coupling on either side.

MOTION DIRECTION IS REVERSED — the headline defect. Orig: bands are born at the strip centre and travel OUTWARD to both ends. Port: bands are born at both ends and travel INWARD to the centre. Measured on the left half by tracking the orange band (orig target (76,13,0), port target (255,122,0)) at 0.2 s spacing over 20 s at 20 fps: orig goes 11,10,9,8,8,7,6,5,4,3,2,1,0 (t=0..2.4 s) then respawns at px 27 near centre; port goes 17,18,19,19,20,21,22,22,23,24,25,25,26,27,28 (t=0..2.8 s) then respawns at px 0 at the edge.

The same reversal is unmistakable in the 240 s / 2 fps survey waterfalls: orig-.png is a stack of '^' chevrons (apex up = feature at centre first, edges later = outward); port.png is a stack of 'V' chevrons (edges first, centre later = inward).

CYCLE PERIOD DIFFERS ~18%. Whole-frame self-correlation of the t=0 frame against 0.2 s-spaced dumps over 20 s: orig peaks at lag 6.6 s (corr 0.988, second peak 13.2 s); port peaks at 7.8-7.9 s (corr 0.952 at 7.8, 0.986 at 15.8). Equivalent band speeds: orig ~4.5 px/s outward, port ~3.85 px/s inward on the 60 px default rig. Port is 1.18x too slow.

BRIGHTNESS IS ~5x TOO HIGH ON THE PORT. meanBrightness avg 7.3 (orig) vs 35.8 (port), identical at 6 s, 60 s, 240 s and in the --skip 60 late window. Peak channel value: orig 76 (the orange stripe), port 255.

Per-stripe ratio port/orig is NOT a single scale factor: orange 3.36x, pink 3.34x, red 4.04x, yellow 4.04x, light-blue 3.8x — but white 15x, green 12.5x, blue 12.5x, purple 12.5x, brown 12x. So on the original the green/blue/purple/white/brown stripes sit at 1-2/255 and are effectively invisible (the pattern reads as dim orange/pink/red/yellow chevrons on black), while on the port every flag stripe is clearly visible. The port's dim-stripe ramp is roughly 4x too shallow on top of the 3.35x absolute overscale.

Hue/order fidelity is good where visible: orig orange hue ~10 deg vs port ~29 deg, orig yellow ~36 deg vs port ~50 deg (port hues are closer to the nominal flag hex), pink ~335 vs ~329 deg, red/green/blue/purple hues agree. The port is slightly less red-shifted than the original in the orange/yellow region.

Single regime only — no modes. The 60 s / 5 fps and 240 s / 2 fps surveys show one uniform chevron texture on both sides end to end, with no banding boundaries, palette walk or cadence change; a --skip 60 run reproduces the 6 s baseline stats exactly on both sides.
feedback: PRIMARY FIX: reverse the propagation direction. The original emits a new colour band at the strip CENTRE and pushes it outward to both ends (waterfall reads as stacked '^' chevrons); the port emits at both ENDS and pulls inward to the centre (stacked 'V'). The colour cycle order in time is already correct and identical on both sides (purple -> blue -> green -> yellow -> orange -> red -> white -> pink -> light-blue -> brown -> black, repeating) — only the sign of the spatial travel term is wrong.
SPEED: the port is too slow. Original completes one full 11-band cycle in 6.6 s (~4.5 px/s on a 60 px strip); the port takes 7.8-7.9 s (~3.85 px/s). Multiply the port's animation rate by ~1.18.
BRIGHTNESS: the port's peak channel is 255 where the original's is 76 — scale the whole output down by ~0.30 (orig mean brightness 7.3 vs port 35.8).

STRIPE BRIGHTNESS RAMP: after the global 0.30 rescale the bright stripes land correctly (orange 255*0.30=76, pink 127*0.30=38) but the dim ones would still be ~4x too bright (green would be 7.5 where the original is 2, white 9 where the original is 2, brown 3.6 where the original is 1). The original applies a much steeper falloff across the flag: relative to orange it holds pink at 0.50, red/yellow at 0.33, light-blue at 0.13, and white/green/blue/purple at 0.026, brown at 0.013. The port's corresponding relatives are 0.50, 0.40, 0.15, 0.098-0.118, 0.047. Match the original's steeper ramp (roughly an extra gamma on the low end) as well as the global scale.

MINOR: orig orange sits at hue ~10 deg and yellow at ~36 deg; the port's are ~29 and ~50 deg. The port's hues are the more 'correct' flag colours, but if the goal is matching the original, warm the orange/yellow stripes ~15-20 deg toward red.

DO NOT CHANGE: band count (11 per half), band width (strip/22 px), the i<->60-i mirror about the centre, resolution independence, fps independence, determinism, and the empty control surface — all of these already match the original exactly.
